messages.subject: Question regarding lavPredict
parts:
Greetings,

A paper that I am working on requires predicting the achievement scores for each time point of a growth curve model with time-invariant predictors of the intercept and slope.  What I would like to know is how lavPredict is providing predictions for this type of model.  I am using the type="ov" command, and would like to know if lavPredict is estimating the observed variables using the full model with time-invariant predictors.  

Thanks

David

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Question regarding lavPredict
parts:
On 03/20/2018 12:28 AM, David Kaplan wrote:
> the type="ov" command, and would like to know if lavPredict is
> estimating the observed variables using the full model with
> time-invariant predictors.

What lavPredict() does (when type="ov") is the following:

1) it predicts factorscores in the usual way: we compute a 'factor score
weights matrix' (say, 'FSC', based on the model matrices), and then we
get factor scores by computing Y %*% t(FSC) (where Y is the data).

2) next, when type = "ov", we simply multiply the factor scores by the
factor loadings to get values for all the indicators

This can be useful for diagnostics (and it is used when you ask for
case-wise residuals), but this was never intended for 'prediction'.

Yves.
